step1_analysis.circuit_type: Filtered Bias Circuit / Current Mirror Reference
step1_analysis.description: A diode-connected NMOS with a PMOS transistor acting as a large resistor in the feedback path. It generates a DC bias voltage while low-pass filtering high-frequency noise from the reference current, commonly used to bias VCO tail current sources without requiring passive inductors.

paper_reference.title: The Impact of Device Type and Sizing on Phase Noise Mechanisms

phase_noise_1mhz.description: Phase noise at 1 MHz offset (Full VCO metric)

sky130_expected.reasoning: Requires the full VCO circuit to measure. The filtered bias circuit helps achieve this low phase noise by suppressing AM-PM conversion.

phase_noise_100khz.description: Phase noise at 100 kHz offset (Full VCO metric)

sky130_expected.reasoning: Requires the full VCO circuit to measure.
The bias circuit consumes only a small fraction of the full VCO's 13.5 mW power.

bias_voltage.description: DC bias voltage generated at N2

sky130_expected.reasoning: Based on SKY130 NMOS parameters at 100uA reference current.

filter_cutoff_freq.description: -3dB cutoff frequency of the bias filter

sky130_expected.reasoning: The PMOS acts as a large resistor. The cutoff frequency depends heavily on the load capacitance (C_gs of the tail transistor).

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure the DC bias voltage, power consumption, and AC low-pass filtering characteristics of the bias circuit.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Filtered Bias Circuit Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u

XM1 N3 N2 N1 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 N2 N1 N3 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}

VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VGND N1 0 0

* Reference current with AC component for filter analysis
Iref VDD N3 DC 100u AC 1u

* Load capacitance representing the tail transistor gate
Cload N2 0 1p

.control
* DC Operating Point
op
let bias_voltage = v(N2)
let power_consumption = 1.8 * 100u
print bias_voltage power_consumption

* AC Analysis for Filter Cutoff
ac dec 100 1k 1G
let filter_gain = vdb(N2) - vdb(N3)
meas ac dc_gain find filter_gain at=1k
let target_gain = dc_gain - 3
meas ac filter_cutoff_freq when filter_gain=target_gain fall=1

* Transient Analysis
tran 1n 1u
meas tran v_n2_max max v(N2)
meas tran v_n2_min min v(N2)

quit
.endc
